problem_text:
A logistics company is selecting cargo containers to load onto a transport vehicle. Available containers are:
* Container 1: weight 4 tons, revenue $91
* Container 2: weight 23 tons, revenue $101
* Container 3: weight 30 tons, revenue $158
* Container 4: weight 40 tons, revenue $257
* Container 5: weight 42 tons, revenue $170
* Container 6: weight 50 tons, revenue $162

* Container 9: weight 32 tons, revenue $28
* Container 10: weight 45 tons, revenue $244
* Container 11: weight 28 tons, revenue $147
* Container 12: weight 24 tons, revenue $109
* Container 13: weight 1 ton, revenue $200
* Container 14: weight 16 tons, revenue $280
* Container 15: weight 8 tons, revenue $115
* Container 16: weight 25 tons, revenue $167
* Container 17: weight 11 tons, revenue $25
* Container 18: weight 27 tons, revenue $200
* Container 19: weight 40 tons, revenue $244
* Container 20: weight 12 tons, revenue $218
* Container 21: weight 19 tons, revenue $109
* Container 22: weight 36 tons, revenue $147
* Container 23: weight 23 tons, revenue $170
* Container 24: weight 25 tons, revenue $224
* Container 25: weight 47 tons, revenue $67
* Container 26: weight 25 tons, revenue $115
* Container 27: weight 3 tons, revenue $116
* Container 28: weight 32 tons, revenue $182
* Container 29: weight 33 tons, revenue $126
* Container 30: weight 36 tons, revenue $137
The vehicle has a maximum payload capacity of 562 tons. Select the combination of containers that maximizes total revenue without exceeding this weight limit. Each container must be either fully loaded or left behind.
